subject: MAP: POC activation — API keys, org bootstrap, IP allowlist & VPC peering
messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sam Lee <sam.lee@syncwell.ai>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com
Date: Mon, 18 Jun 2028 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: MAP draft + kickoff items — POC activation (keys, org, allowlist, peering)

Hi Sam —

Great to be moving this forward. Attached is a lightweight MAP draft that lays out the minimum activation work to get a production-like POC running on Redwood: API key issuance, org bootstrap, IP allowlist, and VPC peering. High level ask list below so we can align at kickoff:

- Org setup: create SyncWell Redwood org and invite two teammates (engineer and infra point)
- API keys: request production POC keys and a short-lived staging key for smoke tests
- IP allowlist: provide CIDR blocks for agent egress (two ranges preferred) and list of static NAT IPs
- VPC peering: identify VPC name, account/project id, and who will own the peering request
- Timing: canonical close target = 3 weeks from signature; aim to finish network & keys in week 1

I've attached: MAP-draft-syncwell-v1.pdf (roadmap + responsibilities). For the kickoff I'd like to propose: Wed Jun 20 10:00 AM PT — 30 min. If that works, I’ll send calendar invite and include the VPC prerequisites doc.

Thanks — we’ll make sure the activation has a short fallback path (temporary allowlist window) so you can run initial tests without waiting on peering.

Best,
Olga Petrov
Enterprise Account Exec, Redwood Inference
olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com
Attachments: MAP-draft-syncwell-v1.pdf

Subject: Re: MAP draft + kickoff items — POC activation (keys, org, allowlist, peering)

Hi Olga —

Thanks — Wed 6/20 10am PT works for our team. A couple quick clarifications before the call so we can pull the right folks:

1) VPC peering: does Redwood require cross-account peering (we're on AWS) or is a transit/VPN option supported for the initial POC? Our infra team prefers avoiding cross-account peering if possible.
2) IP allowlist: will we need to expose a long list of Redwood IPs at the firewall, or can you support a small set of egress NAT IPs for the POC?
3) Do you have an example of the required IAM/service account roles for the peering and for any appliance/service accounts you expect to provision?

Looping procurement for any paperwork. See you on Wed.

—Sam
Sam Lee, Head of Engineering, SyncWell AI
sam.lee@syncwell.ai

Subject: Re: MAP draft + kickoff items — POC activation (keys, org, allowlist, peering)

Hi Sam —

Quick answers ahead of the call:

- VPC peering vs VPN: for the POC we support both. Cross-account VPC peering is preferred for production-like latency; if you want to avoid peering initially we can provision a short-lived VPN (managed tunnel) so you can run integration tests while peering is scheduled.

- IP allowlist: for the canonical serving endpoints we provide a small set of static egress NAT IPs (5 addresses) which are sufficient for most customers. If you plan to use private peering, we ask for the CIDR of your peering subnet (example: 10.20.0.0/22) so we can set route targets.

- IAM / service account: minimal requirements for AWS peering are documented in the attached vpc-peering-template.txt (we include the policy statements we request to create the peering connection and the route table update role). For the Redwood service account we only need permission to accept peering and to read VPC metadata — nothing that modifies your workloads.

Attachment: vpc-peering-template.txt (policy + step checklist)

On the call we'll walk through: who owns the peering ticket, timelines (peering typically 2–3 business days once permissions are granted), and the fallback window (we can open an allowlist for a rolling 72-hour test window if you want immediate access).

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachments: vpc-peering-template.txt

Team —

Thanks for the handoff. Two asks for the kickoff:

1) Present a recommended close cadence in the MAP: week 0 (signature), week 1 (network & API keys), week 2 (integration + smoke tests), week 3 (canary & acceptance). Call out any optional steps (VPN fallback, temporary allowlist window).
2) Prepare a short rollback/fallback plan: if peering is delayed beyond 5 business days, we offer a managed VPN + 72hr allowlist window to avoid blocking SyncWell's engineering schedule.

Olga — propose that you include the above as explicit milestones and dates in the MAP and ask Sam to confirm ownership for the peering ticket and the infra contact. Also flag procurement — any paperwork that needs sign-off should be visible on day 0 so lawyers/procurement can triage.

Vivek
VP, Customer Success — Redwood Inference

Sam —

Thanks again on the call this morning. Per the discussion, attached is an updated MAP that includes the activation milestones and the fallback options Vivek requested. Key dates proposed:

- Day 0 (signature): countersign MAP + procurement checklist posted to Drive (link below)
- Day 1–3: org bootstrap + API key issuance (we’ll create both an integration key and a short-lived staging key)
- Day 4–7: network window: either VPC peering or managed VPN setup (if you want no peering initially we will provision VPN for day 4 testing)
- Day 8–12: integration run (smoke tests, auth validation, sample traffic workstreams)
- Day 13–21: canary and acceptance; handover meeting scheduled on Day 21

Action items for SyncWell (please confirm owners):
- Confirm infra point for peering ticket (name + email) — REQUIRED for peering path
- Provide two egress CIDR/NAT IPs (or validate you want Redwood static NAT IPs) — REQUIRED for allowlist window
- Procurement: review attached procurement addendum and flag any gating contract items

Links & attachments: MAP-draft-syncwell-v1.pdf (updated), activation-checkpoints.xlsx (milestones), DocuSign envelope: https://www.docusign.com/en/link/sample-envelope-12345, Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cMAPSyncWell

If you can confirm infra owner and provide the CIDRs by EOD Fri Jun 22, we can keep the proposed Day 1–3 key issuance target. Otherwise we’ll shift network work into week 2.

Thanks — sending updated calendar invites now.

Olga Petrov
Enterprise Account Exec, Redwood Inference
